items.title: Why Gen Z Men Are Rethinking Their 2024 Trump Vote | WSJ
items.author: The Wall Street Journal
items.content:
<article>President Trump was ushered into a second term in office in part by winning over young men, a majority of whom supported him. Two years later, that support has eroded.

Republicans are on the defense heading into the November elections as they grapple with Trump’s low approval ratings with young men and other parts of his 2024 coalition. Democrats are heavily favored to win the House and have a chance at retaking the Senate, according to analysts.

Last year, The Wall Street Journal brought together a group of men under 30 years old who had all voted for Trump to get their grades of his first six months in office. We invited them back just before the 2026 midterm elections to get their perspectives.

items.title: We Went Inside Cuba to See Its Messy Economic Transformation | WSJ
items.author: The Wall Street Journal
items.content:
<article>Cuba is in the midst of its worst economic crisis in decades, as escalating U.S. sanctions and a fuel blockade continue to create shortages of food, fuel, and other basic goods. But as the communist government’s state-run institutions fail, the island’s private sector is beginning to take off, thanks to a wave of reforms that have opened up Cuba’s economy more than at any time since the revolution. 

The Wall Street Journal obtained visas to report in Cuba and see firsthand how these two divergent realities are coming into conflict. Watch WSJ’s on-the-ground look at how Cuba’s deepening crisis has created its own economic boom.

1:00 The transitions from a full state-run economy
